terms.definition: A running chart of one measurement. It shows whether the tool is behaving the way it usually does.
terms.whyItMatters: A point outside the normal pattern is the alarm a supervisor can act on before a lot is scrapped.

terms.definition: The official record of what will be contained now and what will be changed so the same problem does not return.
terms.whyItMatters: Nothing is written to the quality system until a person approves this record.

terms.definition: Scheduled work that services a tool before it fails, such as a clean, a part change, or a check.
terms.whyItMatters: Maintenance in the same week as an alarm can look like the cause even when it is not.

terms.definition: One number for how much good work a tool produced compared with the time it was scheduled to run. It folds in uptime, speed, and good wafers.
terms.whyItMatters: A manager can compare tools without reading each sensor.

terms.definition: The average hours a tool runs before it needs a repair.
terms.whyItMatters: A short gap means the tool is failing often, even if each repair is quick.

terms.definition: The average hours to bring a tool back after it stops.
terms.whyItMatters: A long repair keeps the tool out of production after the failure is already known.

terms.expansion: mean time to repair a quality incident
terms.definition: The average days from a quality incident opening until the fix is in place.
terms.whyItMatters: This is the investigation clock, not the mechanic's repair clock.

terms.definition: A deliberate change to a recipe, a part, or a setting.
terms.whyItMatters: A change just before an alarm is a prime suspect when only the changed tool moved.

terms.definition: The notice that tells the fab an engineering change is approved and when it takes effect.
terms.whyItMatters: The notice dates the change so it can be lined up with the first bad wafer.

terms.definition: The numbered order that authorizes an engineering change.
terms.whyItMatters: The order is the citation that ties a part or recipe change to a specific tool.

terms.definition: The top line on a control chart. Points above it are unusual for this measurement.
terms.whyItMatters: Crossing it is a signal to look, even when the product spec has not been broken yet.

terms.definition: The bottom line on a control chart. Points below it are unusual for this measurement.
terms.whyItMatters: A drop below the line can be as serious as a spike above it.

terms.definition: A score for how comfortably the normal spread of a measurement sits inside its allowed window.
terms.whyItMatters: A low score means the tool is making parts close to the edge even when no single point is an alarm.

terms.definition: Software that watches many sensors at once and groups the pattern into a known kind of fault.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the automatic watch that raises an alarm before an engineer plots one chart.

terms.definition: A quality record that a wafer, a lot, or a tool did not meet its requirement.
terms.whyItMatters: An open report is prior evidence. A missing one means this incident is new.

terms.definition: The money spent because work was not right the first time: scrap, rework, warranty, downtime, and investigation time.
terms.whyItMatters: It turns a technical incident into a cost a manager can compare.

terms.definition: Electrical power at a high frequency that lights and sustains the plasma, or that shakes a clean bath.
terms.whyItMatters: Too much or too little changes etch rate, film quality, or how clean a wafer gets.

terms.definition: How much gas is flowing, measured as if the gas were at standard temperature and pressure.
terms.whyItMatters: The recipe's gas mix is set in these units. A drift changes the chemistry in the chamber.

terms.definition: A very small pressure unit. One thousand millitorr is one torr, about a thousandth of atmospheric pressure.
terms.whyItMatters: Etch recipes run at a set pressure. A step away from it changes how the plasma hits the wafer.

terms.definition: The plate that holds a wafer with an electric charge and controls the wafer's temperature.
terms.whyItMatters: If the chuck temperature wobbles, etch depth and film thickness wobble with it.

terms.definition: The system of record for nonconformance reports and corrective actions.
terms.whyItMatters: The approved fix is written here. The model is not allowed to write it.

terms.definition: The system that records which recipe, lot, and tool configuration actually ran.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the shop-floor record. If it disagrees with the design record, the cause cannot be named yet.

terms.definition: The system that stores the approved design: parts, revisions, and engineering changes.
terms.whyItMatters: It says what should have been installed. The run record says what was installed.

terms.definition: The system that records material lots, suppliers, and what was issued to a tool.
terms.whyItMatters: A new gas or chemical lot that touched several tools points at the material, not one chamber.

terms.definition: The system that records work orders, calibrations, and preventive maintenance.
terms.whyItMatters: An overdue calibration or a same-week service visit is evidence about the equipment.

terms.definition: The money the change is expected to save compared with what it costs to run.
terms.whyItMatters: The figures on this screen are illustrative and synthetic. They are not a customer measurement.

terms.definition: A set of pattern rules for a control chart. They flag unusual runs, not only a single point outside the window.
terms.whyItMatters: A tool can still be inside its spec window and already be drifting.

terms.definition: One point farther than three standard deviations from the average.
terms.whyItMatters: That point is rare for a stable process and is treated as an alarm.

terms.definition: Two of three points farther than two standard deviations from the average, on the same side.
terms.whyItMatters: The pattern can trip while every point is still inside the product window.

terms.definition: Four of five points farther than one standard deviation from the average, on the same side.
terms.whyItMatters: It catches a shift that is smaller than a single-point alarm.

terms.definition: Eight points in a row on one side of the average.
terms.whyItMatters: A long run on one side means the process has moved, even if it has not spiked.

terms.definition: Sensors on the tool that publish measurements automatically.
terms.whyItMatters: This is the channel for an alarm that a chart raised, as opposed to a person typing a report.

terms.definition: The device that meters how much gas enters the chamber.
terms.whyItMatters: A controller that reads high or low changes the recipe without a person touching the setpoint.

terms.definition: The model that reads the evidence pack and drafts a ranking. It does not write to the quality system.
terms.whyItMatters: Violet marks model steps. Cyan marks rules. A person still approves.

terms.definition: The request path the console uses to read or update a record.
terms.whyItMatters: A failed request is shown as-is. The console does not invent a record the service refused.

terms.definition: The written target for this demonstration: what the product must do, and the gates it must pass.
terms.whyItMatters: A blank metric means the gate has not been scored yet. It is not a passing score.

terms.definition: The open-source license for this demonstration. It grants use and does not transfer ownership.
terms.whyItMatters: Ownership stays with Bryan C. Weis and Common Consulting Company.

terms.definition: The numbered work item opened when an alarm or a report needs an engineer.
terms.whyItMatters: The ticket is the human queue. The investigation starts from it.

terms.definition: The case that gathers evidence and, when the evidence is enough, a recommended cause.
terms.whyItMatters: Opening an investigation does not write a fix.

terms.definition: How many wafers the tool finishes in an hour while it is running the current recipe.
terms.whyItMatters: A drop means the tool is slower, even if it has not stopped.

terms.expansion: share of time the tool was ready
terms.definition: The percent of scheduled time the tool was up and able to run.
terms.whyItMatters: This is availability. It does not say whether the wafers were good.

terms.expansion: wafers that passed the first time
terms.definition: The percent of wafers that met the requirement without rework.
terms.whyItMatters: Rework hides in output counts. First-pass yield does not.
